slides.say: JSX looks like HTML. But it is turned into plain JavaScript before it runs.
This JSX means the same as calling create element with a type, some props, and the children.
This explains the capital letter rule. A capital tag passes your function. A lowercase tag passes a string, a built-in HTML tag.

slides.text: JSX and React are separate: JSX is syntax, React is a library. JSX just makes tags easier to read.
slides.say: JSX is a syntax extension, React is a library. Both styles work. JSX just makes it easy to see which closing tag matches which opening tag.
